title: Past Tense: Complete Conjugation and Narration
lede: Conjugate the Arabic past tense for singular, dual and plural persons, integrate weak-verb stems and use completed actions in coherent narratives.

items.feedback: ـتُ marks first-person singular in the past.
The vowel on ـتِ distinguishes feminine singular “you”.
ـوا marks masculine/mixed third-person plural in the past.

options: Past forms must match person, number and gender.
Every past verb ends with ت.
Arabic always requires a separate subject pronoun.
items.feedback: The verb ending often makes the subject clear.

items.prompt: Best opening for a completed event
items.feedback: Past time phrase matches the completed action.
Past form and time sequence agree.

blocks: ## Why this matters لِمَاذَا نُتْقِنُ الْمَاضِي؟
Past tense lets learners describe experiences, journeys, achievements and events—essential content for speaking and writing.
Use the most frequent singular and plural endings.
Conjugate all persons, including dual and feminine plural.
Integrate hollow, doubled and final-weak stems and analyse full agreement.
[callout] Communication target: Tell a connected account in which each past form clearly identifies its subject.
Check your control of the main endings.
Begin with who is being described, then choose the correct ending.
TABLE: Pronoun | Ending | كَتَبَ // هُوَ | — | كَتَبَ // هِيَ | ـَتْ | كَتَبَتْ // هُمَا (m.) | ـَا | كَتَبَا // هُمَا (f.) | ـَتَا | كَتَبَتَا // هُمْ | ـُوا | كَتَبُوا // هُنَّ | ـْنَ | كَتَبْنَ
[callout] Third person starts from the dictionary past form. The ending shows whether the subject is masculine, feminine, singular, dual or plural.
These endings let speakers narrate personal and shared experiences precisely.

TABLE: Pronoun | Ending | دَرَسَ // أَنَا | ـْتُ | دَرَسْتُ // نَحْنُ | ـْنَا | دَرَسْنَا // أَنْتَ | ـْتَ | دَرَسْتَ // أَنْتِ | ـْتِ | دَرَسْتِ // أَنْتُمَا | ـْتُمَا | دَرَسْتُمَا // أَنْتُمْ | ـْتُمْ | دَرَسْتُمْ // أَنْتُنَّ | ـْتُنَّ | دَرَسْتُنَّ
[callout] The three short vowels matter: دَرَسْتُ I studied, دَرَسْتَ you m. studied, دَرَسْتِ you f. studied.
The ending still marks the subject, but the stem may adapt.
The stem shortens before consonant-led endings.
The final weak letter changes shape.
[callout/warning] Ending + stem: Conjugation is not only adding a suffix. First identify the verb family, then attach the correct person ending to the appropriate stem.
## Use the past to tell events
Past tense becomes meaningful through time expressions, sequencing and varied subjects.
[callout] Narrative frame: فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي ... أَوَّلًا ... ثُمَّ ... بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ... أَخِيرًا ...

TABLE: Purpose | Useful past forms | Model // Personal action | ذَهَبْتُ، شَاهَدْتُ، قَرَأْتُ | أَمْسِ قَرَأْتُ مَقَالًا. // Shared experience | زُرْنَا، لَعِبْنَا، رَجَعْنَا | فِي العُطْلَةِ زُرْنَا مِصْرَ. // Report others | فَازُوا، سَافَرَتْ، وَصَلْنَ | فَازُوا بِالْمُبَارَاةِ. // Reaction | أَعْجَبَنِي، فَرِحْتُ، تَعَلَّمْتُ | تَعَلَّمْتُ شَيْئًا جَدِيدًا.
A useful correction explains the form, not only the answer.
The final short vowel identifies the person.
ـتْ is third-person feminine; ـتِ is second-person feminine.
Grammar becomes useful when it helps you understand and communicate.
Read a short biography and identify who performed each action. Use the endings to resolve pronouns that are not written separately.
Listen to a weekend account and create a timeline of completed actions. Record the exact past form used.
Tell a one-minute story using first-person singular, first-person plural and a third-person report.
Repair a narrative with person-ending confusion, inconsistent past time expressions and two irregular stems.
Write a 130–140-word blog entry about a memorable day. Use at least eight different past verbs and at least four different subject endings.
[callout] Model: فِي الأُسْبُوعِ الْمَاضِي ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى مَعْرِضٍ ثَقَافِيٍّ. رَأَيْنَا صُوَرًا جَمِيلَةً، وَقَالَ الْمُرْشِدُ إِنَّ الْمَعْرِضَ يَعْرِضُ تَارِيخَ الْمَدِينَةِ.
[callout] Success checklist: Use sequencing, past time expressions, one hollow verb, one weak verb and both singular and plural subjects.
Plan the verb changes as a timeline, root map or sentence flowchart. Label each form in Arabic.
Underline every past ending and label the subject above it. Then circle any stem change caused by a weak or doubled root.
Use the full past system accurately.
- conjugate regular past verbs for all main persons;
- distinguish similar endings such as ـتُ، ـتَ، ـتِ and ـتْ;
- apply past endings to weak and doubled stems;
- write and speak about completed events coherently.
Return in 3–7 days and repeat the final check without reviewing first. Retrieval, not recognition alone, builds secure verb control.
